t: Light wavelength λ falls on a metal having work function hc/λ₀. Photoelectric effect will take place only if:

The energy of an incident photon of wavelength λ is E = hc/λ. The work function of the metal is Φ = hc/λ₀, where λ₀ is the threshold wavelength.

For photoelectric emission to occur, the energy of the incident photon must be greater than or equal to the work function:
E ≥ Φ
hc/λ ≥ hc/λ₀
1/λ ≥ 1/λ₀
λ ≤ λ₀

Therefore, the wavelength of incident light must be less than or equal to the threshold wavelength λ₀. If λ > λ₀, the photon energy is insufficient to eject electrons, making options (A), (B), and (D) incorrect.
